description.value: In this assessment, students respond to a given design situation by developing a commercial product for a specified target audience. Students follow the design process to analyse user needs and market factors, define a design brief, generate and prototype ideas, and evaluate and refine their solution against developed criteria. They consider materials, systems, manufacturing processes, sustainability, and commercial viability when making design decisions. Students communicate their final designed solution through appropriate representations and justify their decisions, demonstrating innovation, enterprise skills, and effective use of technologies throughout the design process.

resourcesAvailable.value:
Rapid prototyping technologies, including 3D printers and laser cutters, for iterative concept testing and refinement.
Digital project management templates, including Gantt charts, cost-analysis spreadsheets, and design journal frameworks.
Research resources, including market analysis databases, case studies on commercial innovation, and Life Cycle Analysis (LCA) toolkits.
Prototyping and production consumables: high-density foam, corrugated card, 3D printing filament, adhesives, and context-specific raw materials (timbers, acrylics, or metals).
Multimodal presentation hardware and software for the development and delivery of the commercial pitch.

context.value: In this unit, students explore commercial design by examining how products are developed to meet user needs and succeed in competitive markets. Students investigate market analysis, target audiences, product design and manufacturing processes, and basic business principles such as value proposition, cost, and sustainability. Through analysis of existing commercial products and innovation case studies, students develop an understanding of how designers balance functionality, aesthetics, ethical considerations, and commercial viability. The unit emphasises innovation, enterprise skills, and informed decision-making in the development of market-ready designed solutions.

task.value: In this assessment, students respond to a given design situation by developing a commercial product for a specified target audience. Students follow the design process to analyse user needs and market factors, define a design brief, generate and prototype ideas, and evaluate and refine their solution against developed criteria. They consider materials, systems, manufacturing processes, sustainability, and commercial viability when making design decisions. Students communicate their final designed solution through appropriate representations and justify their decisions, demonstrating innovation, enterprise skills, and effective use of technologies throughout the design process.

toComplete.value: To complete this task, you must independently research and analyse a specific consumer gap within a designated market segment to inform the development of a design brief. You will conduct primary market research, such as user surveys or empathy interviews, to synthesise target audience needs and define performance criteria. Using these insights, you must generate multiple design concepts, represent them through 2D and 3D graphical techniques—including orthogonal and rendered views—and select a final concept for development. You are required to create a detailed project management plan, encompassing sequenced action and cost plans, and construct a functional prototype using appropriate materials and manufacturing processes. Throughout the iterative design process, you must document and justify your decision-making in a digital design journal, specifically addressing sustainability, commercial viability, and ethical considerations. Finally, you will present your market-ready solution, articulating your value proposition and design journey in a formal multimodal pitch designed to engage prospective stakeholders.

stimulus.value: See Stimulus at end of task sheet

scaffolding.value: Instruction on conducting market scans and empathy mapping to identify design opportunities. Provision of a design brief template to assist in defining success criteria, constraints, and sustainability considerations. Use of SCAMPER to facilitate divergent ideation and concept development. Structured checkpoints for project management, utilising digital Gantt charts to track production milestones, costs, and risk mitigation. Guided prototyping sessions with access to material testing labs and rapid fabrication tools. Provision of a pitch-deck framework to structure the final multimodal presentation and the articulation of a commercial value proposition. Formative feedback loops through peer critique sessions and teacher conferencing on portfolio drafts. Explicit teaching of life cycle thinking and ethical frameworks to inform material selection and the evaluation of the designed solution.

Your teacher will conduct interviews after submission to clarify or explore aspects of your response.
Your teacher will compare the responses of students who have worked together in groups.
